note: Procedural provisions the drafting engine needs to ground bail / quashing / complaint documents under BNSS (the code that replaced the CrPC on 1 July 2024). Same discipline as offence-kb.json: every `oldRef` is cross-checked against sanhita-map.json by validate-procedure-kb.ts, and every entry is `needs-review` until counsel verifies. Built to correct a live drift — the web doc-schemas said 'Regular bail (Sec 439 BNSS)', but BNSS regular bail is 480 (or 483 for HC/Sessions special powers); 439 was the CrPC number.

entries.sectionTitle: When bail may be taken in case of non-bailable offence
entries.forum: Magistrate (or Court of Session / High Court via BNSS 483)
entries.whenUsed: Accused is in custody and applies for release on bail in a non-bailable offence.
entries.notes: CrPC 437 -> BNSS 480 per sanhita-map.json. For the High Court/Court of Session's special/wider powers to grant bail, cite BNSS 483 (old CrPC 439), NOT 480. The web app's '439 BNSS' label is wrong and should be 480/483.

entries.sectionTitle: Special powers of High Court or Court of Session regarding bail
entries.sectionText: (1) A High Court or Court of Session may direct— (a) that any person accused of an offence and in custody be released on bail, and if the offence is of the nature specified in sub-section (3) of section 480, may impose any condition which it considers necessary for the purposes mentioned in that sub-section; (b) that any condition imposed by a Magistrate when releasing any person on bail be set aside or modified: Provided that the High Court or the Court of Session shall, before granting bail to a person who is accused of an offence which is triable exclusively by the Court of Session or which, though not so triable, is punishable with imprisonment for life, give notice of the application for bail to the Public Prosecutor unless it is, for reasons to be recorded in writing, of opinion that it is not practicable to give such notice. (GAZETTE TEXT PENDING COUNSEL VERIFICATION against BNSS 2023 bare Act.)
entries.forum: Court of Session or High Court
entries.whenUsed: Bail application moved before the Court of Session or High Court invoking their wider bail powers (commonly after a Magistrate's refusal, or directly for graver offences).
entries.notes: CrPC 439 -> BNSS 483 per sanhita-map.json. This is the section to cite when the FORUM is Sessions/HC. Distinct from BNSS 480 (Magistrate-level).

entries.sectionTitle: Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest
entries.forum: Court of Session or High Court
entries.whenUsed: Person apprehends arrest in a non-bailable offence and seeks a pre-arrest bail direction.
entries.notes: CrPC 438 -> BNSS 482 per sanhita-map.json. CAUTION: BNSS 482 (anticipatory bail) must not be confused with CrPC 482 (inherent powers) — under BNSS, inherent powers moved to 528. The number 482 changed meaning between the codes.

entries.sectionTitle: Procedure when investigation cannot be completed in twenty-four hours (default/statutory bail)
entries.whenUsed: Investigation not completed and charge-sheet not filed within the statutory period; accused becomes entitled to bail as of right.
entries.notes: CrPC 167 -> BNSS 187 per sanhita-map.json. Confirm the exact time limits (60/90 days equivalents) and sub-section against the bare Act — BNSS restructured custody provisions.

entries.sectionTitle: Saving of inherent powers of High Court
entries.sectionText: Nothing in this Sanhita shall be deemed to limit or affect the inherent powers of the High Court to make such orders as may be necessary to give effect to any order under this Sanhita, or to prevent abuse of the process of any Court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice. (GAZETTE TEXT PENDING COUNSEL VERIFICATION against BNSS 2023 bare Act.)
entries.whenUsed: Petition to quash an FIR/complaint/proceedings invoking the High Court's inherent powers.
entries.notes: CrPC 482 -> BNSS 528 per sanhita-map.json. Any drafting template still saying 'quashing under Section 482 CrPC' must be updated to 'Section 528 BNSS'.

entries.forum: Officer in charge of a police station
entries.whenUsed: Registration of a First Information Report in a cognizable offence; cited in complaints and bail narratives.
entries.notes: CrPC 154 -> BNSS 173 per sanhita-map.json. BNSS 173 also introduces electronic/zero-FIR provisions — verify sub-sections.

entries.whenUsed: Filing a private complaint before a Magistrate who then examines the complainant on oath.
entries.notes: CrPC 200 -> BNSS 223 per sanhita-map.json. BNSS 223 adds a proviso (opportunity of hearing to the accused in certain cases) — verify before drafting.

entries.sectionTitle: Provision for inquiries and trial being held in the absence of accused in certain cases
entries.sectionText: (1) At any stage of an inquiry or trial under this Sanhita, if the Judge or Magistrate is satisfied, for reasons to be recorded, that the personal attendance of the accused before the Court is not necessary in the interests of justice, or that the accused persistently disturbs the proceedings in Court, the Judge or Magistrate may, if the accused is represented by an advocate, dispense with his attendance and proceed with such inquiry or trial in his absence, and may, at any subsequent stage of the proceedings, direct the personal attendance of such accused. (2) If the accused in any such case is not represented by an advocate, or if the Judge or Magistrate considers his personal attendance necessary, he may, if he thinks fit and for reasons to be recorded by him, either adjourn such inquiry or trial, or order that the case of such accused be taken up or tried separately. (GAZETTE TEXT PENDING COUNSEL VERIFICATION against BNSS 2023 bare Act.)
entries.forum: Magistrate or Court of Session (the court seized of the inquiry/trial)
entries.whenUsed: Accused (represented by an advocate) applies to be exempted from personal attendance at a hearing — e.g. illness, distance, or where presence is not necessary in the interests of justice.
entries.notes: CrPC 317 -> BNSS 355 per sanhita-map.json. Requires the accused to be represented by an advocate; the court records reasons and may direct personal attendance at any later stage. This is the section behind the failed '317 exemption' draft.
